name: tp-ep-e2e-v5-six
claim: Six-rank end-to-end qualification covering the replicated-group arms and the pure unreplicated TP6EP1 arm, CPU-designed, not executed by its author. No NVFP4/EXL3. The four decode case records are copied verbatim from the frozen four-Spark corpus so prompts and checkers are identical across revisions. This revision ADDS two TP6EP1 arms; it does not replace the accepted v4 corpus (sha256 99034171...) that the existing replicated arms bind.

note: Common controls for every six-rank arm. No SPARK_COUNT/SPARK_TP/SPARK_EP is faked here: per-arm topology lives in the config records. The authoritative matched identity is captured per arm with --startup-metadata (see scripts/fixtures/tp-ep-e2e-startup-metadata.template.json). dspark_draft_limit is per config (7 for 2RTX, 5 for the 1RTX single) and must match the arm metadata; it is not a common control. Pure TP6EP1 is one unreplicated group: each of the six ranks holds a disjoint 2304/6 = 384 intermediate slice of EVERY routed expert, so no expert is duplicated and the compact reducer sums six physical rank planes.
2 RTX + 6 Spark, TP2xEP3 = 3 replicated groups of TP2; RTX-local 20, remote 20.
2 RTX + 6 Spark, TP3xEP2 = 2 replicated groups of TP3; RTX-local 20, remote 20.

1 RTX + 6 Spark, TP3xEP2; all 40 routed layers are remote. The coordinator argv must pass --rtx-expert-layers 0 explicitly (an omitted flag defaults to auto and would load RTX experts) and must omit --placement-directory. KV is the initial single auto pool, never the fixed dual pool. Standalone quality + memory/capacity; never speed-compared against a 2-RTX arm.
Pure unreplicated TP6: six disjoint 384-column intermediate slices of every routed expert, one group. Requires the spark_tp6 role in the Spark image.

Release-equivalent single-RTX pure-TP6 arm: the current official 1-RTX placement shape (5 local routed layers, 35 remote, single auto KV pool). The 1-RTX launch path needs a placement directory because local expert layers must hand off to the workers. An all-40-remote variant is a separate measured sidearm, not this baseline.
Same 2 RTX + 6 Spark hardware; speed and quality are comparable with matched controls.
Standalone: quality plus memory/capacity evidence. It is a valid single-RTX throughput report but is not a cross-hardware speedup claim.

reason: unequal rtx_count and remote-layer count; a single-RTX arm is not cross-hardware speed-comparable with a two-RTX arm

note: C1/2/4/8/16 request concurrency x 3 measured repeats plus one warmup, in every six-rank arm.

prompt: Count from 1 to 64, separated by commas. Output only the sequence.

Write a Python function merge_intervals(intervals) that merges overlapping closed integer intervals and returns the merged list sorted ascending. Include type hints for the parameter and the return value, a docstring, and at least three assert examples covering the empty case, an overlapping pair, and chained intervals. Return only one fenced Python code block and no prose.
requirements: one fenced Python code block only
type hints on the parameter and the return value

prompt: Explain virtual memory to a junior programmer in five concise bullet points. Include one concrete page-fault example.

The Python snippet below has an off-by-one bug:

```python
def total(xs):
    t = 0
    for i in range(len(xs) - 1):
        t += xs[i]
    return t
```

In two sentences, explain the bug, then return the corrected function in one fenced Python code block.

note: Sequential C1 prefill; measured with scripts/bench-ds41-prefill-api.py and reported separately from decode.
Sequential C1 prefill; measured with scripts/bench-ds41-prefill-api.py and reported separately from decode.

tier_a_hard: every matched request in both arms completed without error or timeout
both arms pass the same frozen corpus content checks as the four-Spark revision
within-arm greedy output is identical across the three repeats for the same case and concurrency
both arms carry startup_metadata matching their config record and the applied argv
world is 6 with all six physical ranks present exactly once
both arms cover the full case set and the full concurrency x repeat matrix with no holes, duplicates or extra cases
comparison_policy: A comparison is allowed only as declared by a comparison record. Paired arms must share rtx_count, spark_count, resolved_rtx_expert_layers, spark_first_layer and kv_class. A standalone arm passes only with quality results plus actual memory/capacity evidence; without that evidence it is reported partial. A forbidden comparison is rejected with its stated reason, never as a generic identity mismatch.

memory_evidence_schema.domains: Spark and coordinator are separate; never share the reserve

hosts.accounted_resident_bytes: >= expected_spark_resident_bytes (exact TP layer bytes x remote layers)
hosts.source_log: real per-rank log; presence is machine-checked only

spark.kv_pool_class: must equal the config kv_class (g3-paired or single-auto); the actual pool is not fixed

coordinator.device_free_bytes: RTX device free bytes >= runtime_headroom_bytes (never host free memory)
coordinator.source_log: real coordinator log; presence is machine-checked only

memory_evidence_schema.review: set logs_independently_reviewed true only after an independent review of the per-host logs; otherwise the gate stays review-required

note: All TP families are built into the same native library, so both arms record every expert_tp_manifests entry with identical hashes and active_topology carries the per-arm difference. dspark_draft_limit is per config and must match the arm metadata.

six_rank: Full six-Spark hardware (ostrich,dodo,emu,kiwi + rhea,moa) is REQUIRED for every six-rank objective. Two families are approved: the replicated groups (TP2EP3, TP3EP2) and the pure unreplicated TP6EP1 (one group, six disjoint 2304/6=384 intermediate slices of every expert, no expert duplicated). v5 is a strict superset of the accepted v4 arm set: it adds 2rtx6-tp6ep1 and 1rtx6-tp6ep1 and removes nothing. TP3EP2, TP2EP3 and TP6EP1 all still need full runtime qualification, including a per-rank record that the worker loaded its own role and intermediate, before any result is called qualified.
single_rtx: The 1 RTX + 6 Spark TP3EP2 arm runs all 40 routed layers remotely; its memory/capacity qualification is separate from the 2 RTX + 6 Spark fixed-20-layer arms.
build_root: Never build or stage under /mnt/scratch. Use a unique /home/tj/.cache/ds41rt/builds/<task> path on raptor root NVMe and run python3 scripts/assert-build-filesystem.py PATH... before direct builds.
pure_tp6: TP6EP1 requires the extra spark_tp6 role (native role 7, intermediate 384) in the Spark image. An artifact/manifest entry is not proof the running rank loaded it: every rank must report role 7 and intermediate 384 in worker_runtime_role. Delegating live GPU reduction checks to a hardware owner remains required.

note: Same 2 RTX + 6 Spark hardware. Five of six device bytes are unchanged; the candidate trades replicated groups for a single six-way tensor split, so a measured difference is attributable to shard width and plane count, not to hardware.
Standalone: quality plus per-rank memory evidence. No cross-hardware speedup claim.

reason: Different RTX counts and different resolved boundaries; a cross-hardware comparison cannot isolate the TP6 shard geometry.
